Docket 1.3.76

**A scheduled check that fails now leaves something to read.**

When an audit you start yourself goes wrong, Docket writes the details to
~/.docket/crashes/ so the failure can actually be diagnosed. A scheduled
watchlist check kept only the error's name and threw the rest away — which put
the gap in the worst place, because a scheduled check runs unattended at
whatever hour its cadence lands on. The failure least likely to be seen was the
only one leaving nothing behind.

**And a lapsed licence is no longer reported as a failed check.**

If your licence needs attention, a scheduled check used to say "Check failed"
with nothing to act on and nowhere to enter a key. It now opens the activation
panel, the same way an audit you run by hand already did. Nothing worked wrong;
you were simply asked the wrong question.

These are the fourth and fifth things that existed for an audit you run by hand
and were missing from a scheduled one — after live progress, the report each
check keeps, and the ability to stop one. All five were found by comparing the
two paths against each other rather than by waiting for a report.
